subject: pharmacology
title: Skeletal muscle relaxants and ganglion blockers

steps.tx: **Neuromuscular blockers** paralyse skeletal muscle at nicotinic receptors in the neuromuscular junction. These drugs never remove consciousness or pain, so adequate anaesthesia must always accompany paralysis in theatre. **Succinylcholine** mimics acetylcholine and it opens the channel with visible fasciculations before blockade develops. Rocuronium and vecuronium compete silently for the receptor without any initial stimulation phase. The anaesthetist balances onset speed, duration, organ clearance and reversal options in every airway plan.
steps.say: Neuromuscular blockers are drugs that paralyse skeletal muscle at nicotinic receptors in the neuromuscular junction itself. These drugs never remove consciousness or pain so adequate anaesthesia must always accompany paralysis. Succinylcholine is an acetylcholine mimic and it opens the channel with visible fasciculations before blockade. Rocuronium competes silently for the receptor and it produces blockade without initial stimulation.

steps.tx: **Succinylcholine** acts within a minute and it suits rapid sequence intubation in emergencies. Plasma pseudocholinesterase hydrolyses the drug, so inherited enzyme deficiency prolongs apnoea for several hours. The drug raises serum potassium, triggers malignant hyperthermia in susceptible muscle and causes bradycardia and muscle pains. High dose **rocuronium** rivals the onset of succinylcholine in modern practice. Sugammadex encapsulates rocuronium immediately and it has reshaped emergency airway management in many centres.
steps.say: Succinylcholine acts within a minute and it suits rapid sequence intubation in emergency practice. The drug is hydrolysed by plasma pseudocholinesterase so enzyme deficiency prolongs apnoea for several hours afterwards. The drug raises serum potassium and it triggers malignant hyperthermia in susceptible muscle fibres. High dose rocuronium rivals its onset and sugammadex reverses rocuronium almost immediately afterwards.

steps.tx: **Malignant hyperthermia** results from uncontrolled calcium release through defective **ryanodine receptors** in muscle. Succinylcholine or volatile anaesthetics trigger the crisis in genetically susceptible patients during anaesthesia. Sustained contraction produces rigidity, soaring carbon dioxide, hyperthermia and severe metabolic acidosis very quickly. Dantrolene blocks calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum and it acts as the specific antidote. The team removes triggers, cools the patient actively and screens the family afterwards.
steps.say: Malignant hyperthermia results from uncontrolled calcium release through defective ryanodine receptors in muscle fibres. Succinylcholine or volatile anaesthetics trigger the crisis in genetically susceptible patients during anaesthesia. Sustained contraction produces rigidity and it raises carbon dioxide, temperature and acid levels rapidly. Dantrolene blocks calcium release and it acts as the specific antidote for this crisis. The team removes triggers and it cools the patient actively throughout resuscitation.

steps.tx: This molecular image shows a defective **ryanodine receptor** flooding the sarcoplasm with calcium ions. The uncontrolled **calcium flood** drives sustained contraction of actin and myosin filaments below. Muscle rigidity consumes energy rapidly and it produces heat and soaring end tidal carbon dioxide. **Dantrolene** molecules block the defective channel and they cut off the calcium supply at its source. Recognising this mechanism explains why early dantrolene, trigger removal and active cooling decide survival in malignant hyperthermia.
steps.say: This molecular image shows a defective ryanodine receptor flooding the sarcoplasm with calcium ions continuously. The uncontrolled calcium flood drives sustained contraction of the muscle filaments below it. Muscle rigidity consumes energy rapidly and it produces heat and soaring carbon dioxide levels. Dantrolene blocks the defective channel and it cuts off the calcium supply at source. Early dantrolene decides survival because it stops the hypermetabolic process driving the crisis.

steps.tx: The depth of residual block decides which reversal strategy works safely for the patient. **Sugammadex** encapsulates rocuronium and vecuronium and it reverses even deep blockade within minutes. **Neostigmine** helps only after some spontaneous recovery returns, and it needs glycopyrrolate to cover muscarinic effects. Residual paralysis in recovery causes hypoventilation and aspiration, so quantitative monitoring guides safe extubation. A train of four ratio above 0.9 marks the accepted threshold before the tube comes out.
steps.say: The depth of residual block decides which reversal strategy works safely for the patient recovering. Sugammadex encapsulates rocuronium and it reverses even deep blockade within a few minutes reliably. Neostigmine helps only after some spontaneous recovery returns to the neuromuscular junction again. Residual paralysis causes hypoventilation and aspiration so quantitative monitoring guides safe extubation decisions.

steps.tx: Centrally acting **spasmolytics** treat spasticity and they differ completely from surgical muscle relaxants. **Baclofen** activates inhibitory receptors in the spinal cord and it reduces spastic tone in neurology clinics. Tizanidine stimulates alpha 2 receptors centrally, while dantrolene acts peripherally on muscle calcium release. Ganglion blockers such as trimethaphan remain historical because blocking both autonomic limbs causes unpredictable hypotension, ileus and urinary retention. Examination stems separate junction blockers for surgery from spasticity drugs for chronic care.
steps.say: Centrally acting spasmolytics treat spasticity and they differ completely from surgical muscle relaxants used daily. Baclofen reduces spastic tone and tizanidine acts centrally on alpha two receptors in patients. Dantrolene acts peripherally on muscle calcium and it treats chronic spasm as well. Examination stems separate junction blockers for surgery from spasticity drugs for chronic neurological care.
